zh.summary: 從單人本機原型擴大到多人共用時，重新確認角色、資料存取、保存、維運與交接要求，避免把一個可運行的網址當成完整組織系統。
objectives: 指出個人工具與組織共用系統在使用情境與責任上的差異。
區分登入、資料授權與資料保存的要求。
為十人共用情境列出未實作事項及進入下一階段的條件。

readingGuide.goal: 辨識原型變成共用系統時新增的需求與驗證界線。
readingGuide.startingPoint: 沿用本機單人收件原型，假設十位同仁希望共用。
readingGuide.route: 比較使用情境，再分清登入與授權，最後寫出下一階段的需求及驗收條件。
readingGuide.output: architecture.md 的共用需求附錄、權限表與兩條授權情境。

sections.heading: 個人工具與組織系統有什麼不同？
paragraphs: 這一課最重要的觀念是：
一個程式自己用得很好，不代表十個人一起用也會很好。把程式放到網路上，只是讓別人連得進來，不代表它已經能安全地讓大家一起工作。
我們用一個生活故事，理解這背後的軟體工程、資安與系統設計觀念。

sections.heading: 一、為什麼一個人用沒問題，十個人用就可能出事？
paragraphs: 想像你是一位辦公室承辦人，每天要收很多文件。你覺得很麻煩，於是請 AI 幫你寫了一個「文件缺漏檢查系統」。
一開始只有你自己使用，事情很簡單：
你上傳文件，系統幫你檢查有沒有漏掉姓名、日期、附件，然後產生一份報告。
有一天主管說：「這個很好用！可以給整個辦公室使用嗎？」
你請 AI 把程式部署到一個網址，例如：
https://documents.example.com
十個同事都能開啟網站。
看起來大功告成了，對不對？
不一定。
因為接下來可能出現幾種情況：
小明上傳的文件，小美竟然也能看到。
小美可以下載其他承辦人的文件。
兩個人同時修改一份文件，結果其中一人的修改消失了。
伺服器重新啟動後，昨天上傳的資料全部不見。
原本寫程式的人離職，其他人不知道怎麼修復系統。
你會發現，原本的「文件檢查」功能其實沒有壞。
壞的是整個團隊使用這套工具時，沒有建立必要的規則與保護措施。
這就是本課的核心問題。

blocks.caption: 圖 1｜個人工具與十人共用的情境比較
blocks.description: 兩張卡平行比較使用情境；人數本身不是安全判定，擴大使用時要重新確認需求與證據。

items.title: 情境 A：自己使用
items.body: 只有你自己收件、檢查、修改與下載。

items.title: 情境 B：十個人共用
items.body: 大家同時使用，但每個人的工作與權限不同。

sections.heading: 二、從五個面向，理解個人工具與組織系統
paragraphs: 我們可以把組織系統的需求分成五個問題。
這五個面向不一定要用五套不同軟體完成，但設計時都必須考慮。

blocks.caption: 圖 2｜一個能讓多人使用的系統
blocks.description: 不只是功能正確，還要能協作、管理與維護。五個平行面向共同支撐成果；連線不代表先後步驟、已證實因果或已完成驗收。

items.title: 身分
items.body: 誰在使用？

items.title: 權限
items.body: 能做什麼？

items.title: 資料
items.body: 存在哪裡？

items.title: 協作
items.body: 同時操作？

items.title: 維護
items.body: 誰負責？

items.title: 安全、可靠、可交接
items.body: 五個面向共同考慮，不是五套不同軟體或先後流程。

blocks.caption: 表 1｜五個共同考慮的面向
rows: 小明不能刪除別人的文件
系統出問題仍有人能處理
有備份、負責人與交接文件

sections.heading: 三、登入成功，不代表什麼資料都能看
paragraphs: 這裡有兩個非常重要的資安名詞。

blocks.heading: 1. Authentication：身分驗證
paragraphs: 白話文就是：你是誰？
例如小明輸入帳號密碼，系統確認他確實是小明。
這就像你進公司時刷員工證。

blocks.heading: 2. Authorization：授權
paragraphs: 白話文就是：你可以做什麼？
小明雖然是公司員工，但他不一定能進人事室，也不一定能看主管的薪資資料。
換句話說：
身分驗證：確認你是員工。
授權：決定你可以進哪些房間、拿哪些文件。
我們用一個可以點擊的例子來理解。

blocks.caption: 模擬：文件權限檢查
blocks.description: 本教學自行設定：承辦人可讀取、修改、刪除自己的文件；主管為唯讀複核者，可讀兩份但不能修改或刪除。

items.title: 小明（承辦 A）
items.body: 自己的文件 A：可讀、改、刪。文件 B：不可讀、改、刪。

items.title: 小美（承辦 B）
items.body: 自己的文件 B：可讀、改、刪。文件 A：不可讀、改、刪。

items.title: 主管（複核者）
items.body: 文件 A／B：可讀；不可修改或刪除。

blocks.heading: 從角色走到每一份文件的授權
paragraphs: 你可以試試看，把登入身分切換成小美，再選擇讀取文件 A。
這個設計背後還有一個進階觀念：
權限不只是看角色，也可能要看「這筆資料是誰的」。
例如：
RBAC（Role-Based Access Control）：根據角色決定權限。
資源層級授權（Resource-level Authorization）：針對每一份文件檢查誰有權存取。
在真正的系統中，通常需要把兩者結合。例如「你是承辦人」還不夠，還要判斷「這份文件是不是你負責的」。

blocks.heading: 重要：把按鈕藏起來，不等於權限安全
paragraphs: 假設小美的畫面沒有「刪除文件」按鈕，是不是就代表她不能刪除文件？
不一定。
有些人可能不透過網頁按鈕，而是直接向系統的 API 發送刪除請求。
所以真正重要的是：負責執行操作的伺服器，也必須重新檢查權限。
這是前端 UI 與後端安全控制的重大差別。

sections.heading: 四、多人同時使用，會產生什麼問題？
paragraphs: 我們再看一個常見的情境。
假設小明與小美都獲得授權，可以修改同一份文件。
本節是另一個合成情境，另外授權兩人修改同一份文件；與上一節「承辦人只操作自己文件」的固定模擬規則分開。
兩人同時修改同一份資料
09:00 小明打開文件，看到「缺少簽名」。
09:01 小美打開同一份文件，也看到「缺少簽名」。
09:02 小明修改成「已補簽名」，並儲存。
09:03 小美根據舊畫面修改其他欄位，再儲存整份資料。
可能的結果：小明的修改被蓋掉。
因為小美儲存時仍使用舊版本，可能把小明剛完成的更新覆寫。
這類問題叫做 Lost Update（更新遺失），屬於 Concurrency（並行操作）的議題。
解法可以是：每份文件記錄版本號碼。小明修改後版本從 1 變成 2，小美再試圖用版本 1 儲存時，系統會偵測衝突，請她重新確認，而不是直接覆蓋。
這也是為什麼「我自己測試沒有問題」不能證明「多人一起用沒有問題」。
技術補充：版本比對與更新必須在伺服器／資料層以原子操作或交易一起保證；只在前端先比較版本、再獨立寫入，仍可能發生競爭。

blocks.caption: 圖 3｜兩位已授權承辦人仍可能發生更新遺失
blocks.description: 編號代表本合成案例的時間順序。版本衝突需由伺服器／資料層處理；此圖沒有執行實際並行測試。

items.title: 09:00｜小明讀取版本 1
items.body: 看到「缺少簽名」。

items.title: 09:01｜小美讀取版本 1
items.body: 同樣看到「缺少簽名」。

items.title: 09:02｜小明儲存成版本 2
items.body: 內容改為「已補簽名」。

items.title: 09:03｜小美仍用版本 1 儲存
items.body: 若系統無聲覆寫，就可能遺失小明更新；正確設計應偵測衝突，請重新確認。

sections.heading: 五、資料存在哪裡？重開機後還在嗎？
paragraphs: 想像你拿一張紙寫東西，有兩種方式。
第一種，你寫在白板上。白板擦掉，內容就沒了。
第二種，你寫在正式文件裡並存檔，重新打開還可以看。
軟體裡也有類似差別。
Memory（記憶體）：程式執行時暫時放資料的地方。通常程式結束，資料就不再保留。
Persistent Storage（持久化儲存）：例如經妥善設定的資料庫或持久磁碟，讓資料在程式結束之後仍然保存。
Backup（備份）：額外保存可用的資料副本，降低誤刪、故障等造成的損失。
Restore（還原）：真正把資料從備份恢復出來。
要注意的是，資料存在資料庫，不代表已經有備份；有備份，也不代表已經證明可以還原。
例如文件收件系統收到一百份重要文件。如果伺服器故障，必須知道如何把資料救回來，不能只依靠當初開發工具的那個人。

sections.heading: 六、HTTPS 能解決這些問題嗎？
paragraphs: 不能全部解決。
假設你使用 HTTPS 連到文件系統。
HTTPS 的作用，主要是保護資料在網路傳送時的機密性、完整性，以及在憑證驗證正確的條件下協助確認伺服器身分。
但 HTTPS 不會幫你決定小美能不能看小明的文件。
可以這樣記：
它們不是互相替代的技術，而是解決不同層次的問題。

blocks.caption: 表 2｜不同層次的保護機制
rows: 資料傳送途中會不會被竊聽或篡改？
現在使用系統的人是誰？
這個人能操作哪些文件？
資料遺失時能不能救回？
多人修改會不會互相覆蓋？

sections.heading: 七、怎麼證明「十個人真的可以一起使用」？
paragraphs: 這裡要接回前兩堂 AASE 課程的精神：
AI 說它做好了，不等於我們已經驗證完成。
軟體工程常使用 Given–When–Then，把需求寫成可以測試的條件。
例如：
其中，拒絕未授權操作的測試，稱為 Negative Test（負向測試）。
這很重要：不能只測試「合法的人能不能成功」，還要測試「不該成功的人，會不會被確實阻止」。
每個測試都應保留實際執行的證據，例如測試結果、日誌或可檢查的紀錄。只有寫出測試案例，仍不能宣稱已經通過。

blocks.caption: 表 3｜共用需求的驗收情境
rows: 小明讀取自己的文件 A
小美讀取未獲授權的文件 A
兩人同時修改同份文件
不會無聲覆蓋他人的更新
已確認儲存的資料仍存在
能夠恢復指定版本的資料

sections.heading: 八、如果現在只有一個 Streamlit 原型，應該怎麼做？
paragraphs: 不需要馬上建立複雜的企業級系統。
先分清楚三種階段：
階段一：個人原型
一個人在本機，使用合成資料，先驗證文件缺漏檢查功能。
階段二：受控多人測試
定義角色、資料隔離、存取規則，讓少數測試帳號執行允許與拒絕的操作。
階段三：組織正式使用
確認真實資料的使用規則，處理資料持久化、備份還原、多人協作、權限管理及維護交接，並取得驗證證據。
這三個階段不代表每個專案都要花很多錢或建立龐大的基礎設施。系統應該依照使用人數、資料敏感程度、失效後果和組織需求，採用相稱的設計。
教材目前的 Streamlit 程式仍是單人、合成資料的本機原型。不能因為 Streamlit 可以部署到網路，就假設它已經具備正式帳號、資料隔離、多人授權與持久資料庫。
多人身分、授權、持久資料庫與備份還原仍屬待實作／待驗證的需求；本課模擬不是這些控制的實作。

sections.heading: 九、把前三堂課連在一起
paragraphs: 三堂課其實形成一個完整的軟體工程思考方式：
先定義成果 → 分配責任 → 設計使用規則 → 執行測試 → 用證據確認可交付。

blocks.caption: 表 4｜前三堂課的問題
rows: 我們到底要幫使用者解決什麼問題？
AI 可以做什麼？人類必須確認什麼？
當更多人使用時，系統是否仍然安全、正確、可靠？

sections.heading: 十、理解檢核
paragraphs: 以下三題可以幫你確認是否真正理解本課，而不只是記住名詞。先自行判斷，再展開本頁的參考答案；本站不提交答案、自動批改或記錄成績。
這一課最值得帶走的判斷標準是：軟體是否準備好讓團隊使用，不能只看功能會不會動，還要看不同的人能否在正確的權限下，安全且可靠地完成工作。

exercise.environment: 文字編輯器與虛構 A、B、複核者三種角色；不建立真實帳號或共用服務。
steps: 在 architecture.md 列出單人原型目前已具備及未實作的能力。
用合成資料 A、B 畫一張角色—資料—操作權限表，將未確認的規則標為假設。
寫一條允許讀取與一條拒絕讀取的 Given／When／Then，說明應在哪裡檢查權限。
列出資料保存、同時使用、備份及維運的待確認問題，指定下一步由誰核對。
exercise.expected: 一份共用版需求差異表、兩條授權情境與清楚的進入下一階段條件。
exercise.check: 同儕能分清已在原型實作的完整性規則，與尚未實作的多人授權要求；沒有執行時不標示測試通過。
exercise.cleanup: 只保留合成角色與資料代號；不要為紙上練習分享實際資料或改動正式系統權限。

en.summary: When a local single-user prototype becomes shared software, revisit roles, data access, retention, operations and handoff rather than treating a working URL as a complete organizational system.
objectives: Identify differences in use and responsibility between personal tools and shared organizational systems.
Distinguish login, data authorization and data retention requirements.
List unimplemented work and conditions for the next stage of a ten-user shared scenario.

readingGuide.goal: Identify new requirements and verification boundaries when a prototype becomes a shared system.
readingGuide.startingPoint: Start with the local single-user intake prototype and suppose ten colleagues want to share it.
readingGuide.route: Compare use contexts, distinguish login from authorization, then write requirements and acceptance conditions for the next stage.
readingGuide.output: A shared-use appendix in architecture.md, a permission matrix and two authorization scenarios.

sections.heading: How Do Personal Tools Differ from Organizational Systems?
paragraphs: The central idea of this lesson is:
A program that works well for one person does not automatically work well for ten. Putting it online provides a reachable entry point, not proof that people can work together safely.
Use an everyday story to explore the software engineering, security and system-design questions behind this distinction.

sections.heading: 1. Why Might Ten Users Encounter Problems That One User Does Not?
paragraphs: Imagine handling many incoming documents at an office. To reduce repetitive work, you ask AI to create a missing-document checking system.
At first, you are its only user, so the workflow appears simple:
You upload documents, the system checks for missing names, dates and attachments, and it generates a report.
One day a supervisor says, “This is useful! Can the whole office use it?”
You ask AI to deploy it at an address such as:
https://documents.example.com
Ten colleagues can open the website.
Is the job complete?
Not necessarily.
Several problems may appear:
Xiaomei can see documents uploaded by Xiaoming.
Xiaomei can download documents belonging to other administrators.
Two people edit the same document, and one person’s changes disappear.
After the server restarts, yesterday’s uploads are gone.
The original developer leaves, and nobody else knows how to recover the system.
The document-checking feature itself may still work.
The missing pieces are the rules and protections needed when a team uses the tool.
That is the central problem of this lesson.

blocks.caption: Figure 1 | Compare a personal tool with shared use by ten people
blocks.description: The cards compare scenarios in parallel. Headcount alone does not determine security; expanded use needs revised requirements and evidence.

items.title: Scenario A: personal use
items.body: You alone receive, check, edit and download documents.

items.title: Scenario B: ten people sharing
items.body: People use the system at the same time, with different tasks and permissions.

sections.heading: 2. Five Dimensions of Personal Tools and Organizational Systems
paragraphs: Organizational-system needs can be examined through five questions.
These dimensions need not be implemented by five separate products, but each needs consideration during design.

blocks.caption: Figure 2 | A system that supports multiple users
blocks.description: Beyond correct features, it needs collaboration, management and maintenance. The five parallel dimensions jointly support the outcome. Lines do not show a sequence, proven causation or completed acceptance.

items.title: Identity
items.body: Who is using it?

items.title: Permissions
items.body: What may they do?

items.title: Data
items.body: Where is it stored?

items.title: Collaboration
items.body: Working at the same time?

items.title: Maintenance
items.body: Who is responsible?

items.title: Safe, reliable, ready for handoff
items.body: Consider the five dimensions together; they are not five separate products or sequential steps.

blocks.caption: Table 1 | Five dimensions to consider together
rows: Decide what this person may do.
Xiaoming cannot delete another person’s documents.
Changes do not overwrite each other.
Keep someone able to handle failures.
Backups, an owner and handoff documentation.

sections.heading: 3. Logging In Does Not Grant Access to Every Record
paragraphs: Two security terms are important here.

blocks.heading: 1. Authentication
paragraphs: Who are you?
For example, Xiaoming enters account credentials and the system verifies his identity.
This is like presenting an employee badge when entering a company.

blocks.heading: 2. Authorization
paragraphs: What may you do?
Being an employee does not necessarily allow Xiaoming into personnel records or give him access to a supervisor’s salary information.
In other words:
Authentication establishes the employee identity.
Authorization determines which rooms and documents that identity may access.
Use the interactive example below.

blocks.caption: Simulation: document permission checking
blocks.description: Teaching policy: administrators may read, edit and delete their own documents. The supervisor is a read-only reviewer who can read both documents but cannot edit or delete either.

items.title: Xiaoming (Administrator A)
items.body: Own document A: read, edit and delete. Document B: no read, edit or delete.

items.title: Xiaomei (Administrator B)
items.body: Own document B: read, edit and delete. Document A: no read, edit or delete.

items.title: Supervisor (Reviewer)
items.body: Documents A/B: read only; no editing or deletion.

blocks.heading: From roles to authorization for each document
paragraphs: Try switching to Xiaomei and requesting to read document A.
There is a further design idea here:
Permission can depend on who owns the record as well as the role.
For example:
RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) determines permissions from roles.
Resource-level authorization checks access to each individual document.
Real systems commonly need both. Being an administrator is not enough; the system also needs to check whether the document is assigned to that person.

blocks.heading: Important: hiding a button does not enforce secure authorization
paragraphs: If Xiaomei’s screen has no delete button, does that establish that she cannot delete a document?
Not necessarily.
Someone may send a delete request directly to an API without using a webpage button.
The server that performs the operation must check authorization again.
That is a critical distinction between frontend UI and backend enforcement.

sections.heading: 4. What Can Go Wrong When People Work at the Same Time?
paragraphs: Consider another common situation.
Assume Xiaoming and Xiaomei are both authorized to edit the same document.
This is a separate synthetic case that explicitly authorizes both people to edit the same document; it is distinct from the preceding simulation’s fixed owner-only administrator policy.
Two people edit the same record:
09:00: Xiaoming opens the document and sees “signature missing.”
09:01: Xiaomei opens the same document and also sees “signature missing.”
09:02: Xiaoming changes it to “signature supplied” and saves.
09:03: Xiaomei edits another field using the old screen and saves the whole record.
Xiaoming’s update may be overwritten.
Xiaomei is saving an older version, which may replace the update Xiaoming just made.
This is a lost update, a concurrency issue.

One approach is to store a version number with each document. After Xiaoming saves, version 1 becomes version 2. If Xiaomei tries to save version 1, the system detects a conflict and requests review instead of silently overwriting the newer record.
That is why “it worked when I tested it alone” does not establish safe shared use.

Technical note: version comparison and update must be guaranteed together by an atomic operation or transaction at the server/data layer. Checking in the frontend and then writing separately can still race.

blocks.caption: Figure 3 | Two authorized users can still lose an update

items.body: She also sees “signature missing.”

sections.heading: 5. Where Is the Data, and Does It Survive a Restart?
paragraphs: Think of two ways to record information.
You can write on a whiteboard. Once it is erased, the contents are gone.
Or you can save a formal document and reopen it later.
Software has a similar distinction.
Memory temporarily holds data while a program runs. Data held only there usually does not survive program termination.
Persistent storage, such as an appropriately configured database or persistent disk, retains data after the program ends.
Backup means keeping additional usable copies to reduce loss from deletion, failures and similar events.
Restore means actually recovering data from a backup.
A database does not establish that a backup exists, and a backup does not establish that restoration has been demonstrated.
If an intake system receives 100 important documents and the server fails, recovery needs a known method rather than dependence on the original developer alone.

sections.heading: 6. Does HTTPS Solve These Problems?
paragraphs: Not all of them.
Suppose you connect to the document system over HTTPS.
HTTPS primarily protects confidentiality and integrity in transit and, when certificates are correctly validated, helps authenticate the server.
It does not decide whether Xiaomei may read Xiaoming’s document.
Keep the mechanisms separate:
They address different layers and do not replace one another.

blocks.caption: Table 2 | Protection mechanisms address different problems
rows: Can data in transit be eavesdropped on or tampered with?
Which documents may this identity act on?
Can simultaneous edits overwrite one another?

sections.heading: 7. How Can We Verify That Ten People Can Work Together?
paragraphs: Return to the principle established in the first two AASE lessons:
An AI completion claim does not establish completed verification.
Software engineering often uses Given–When–Then to express requirements as testable conditions.
For example:
A test that rejects an unauthorized action is a negative test.
Test whether authorized users succeed and whether users who should not succeed are actually blocked.
Each test needs actual execution evidence, such as results, logs or inspectable records. Writing a test case alone does not establish that it passed.

blocks.caption: Table 3 | Acceptance scenarios for shared use
rows: Xiaoming reads his own document A.
Xiaomei reads document A without authorization.
Two users edit the same document.
Do not silently overwrite another person’s update.
Previously confirmed saved data remains available.

sections.heading: 8. What Should We Do with a Single-User Streamlit Prototype?
paragraphs: There is no need to immediately build a complicated enterprise system.
Distinguish three stages:
Stage 1: personal prototype
One person uses synthetic data locally to check the missing-document feature.
Stage 2: controlled multi-user testing
Define roles, data isolation and access rules, then have a small set of test accounts exercise both allowed and denied operations.
Stage 3: organizational production use
Confirm real-data usage rules, persistence, backup and restore, collaboration, permission management and maintenance handoff, with corresponding verification evidence.

These stages do not require every project to be expensive or use large infrastructure. Choose a proportionate design based on user numbers, data sensitivity, failure consequences and organizational needs.

The course’s Streamlit program remains a local, single-user prototype with synthetic data. Deployability alone does not establish production accounts, data isolation, multi-user authorization or a persistent database.
Multi-user identities, authorization, persistent databases and backup/restore remain requirements awaiting implementation or verification. This lesson’s simulation does not implement those controls.

sections.heading: 9. Connecting the First Three Lessons
paragraphs: The three lessons form a connected software engineering approach:
Define outcomes → assign responsibilities → design usage rules → execute tests → use evidence to confirm deliverable scope.

blocks.caption: Table 4 | Questions from the first three lessons
rows: Which user problem are we solving?
What can AI do, and what must people confirm?
M01-03 | Personal tools and organizational systems
Does the system remain safe, correct and reliable as more people use it?

sections.heading: 10. Understanding Check
paragraphs: The three questions below check understanding rather than terminology alone. Answer first and then expand the reference explanations; this site does not submit, automatically grade or record answers.
Judge readiness for team use by whether different people can complete their work safely and reliably under appropriate permissions, as well as whether the feature runs.

exercise.environment: A text editor and fictional roles A, B and reviewer. Do not create real accounts or a shared service.
steps: List the prototype’s implemented and unimplemented capabilities in architecture.md.
Use synthetic records A and B to create a role–data–action permission matrix, marking unconfirmed rules as assumptions.
Write one allowed-read and one denied-read Given/When/Then scenario and identify where permission checks belong.
List questions about retention, simultaneous use, backups and operations, assigning who should check them next.
exercise.expected: A shared-use requirements comparison, two authorization scenarios and clear conditions for the next stage.
exercise.check: A peer can distinguish implemented completeness rules from unimplemented shared-user authorization. Do not mark tests passed without execution.
exercise.cleanup: Keep only synthetic roles and record identifiers. Do not share actual data or change production permissions for a tabletop exercise.

zh.prompt: 小明和小美都能登入同一套系統，但小美嘗試讀取小明的私人文件。最主要應由哪一項機制決定是否拒絕？
rationales: HTTPS 保護傳輸，不決定每份文件的存取權。
登入辨識身分，不自動授權讀取別人的文件。
C：授權須依身分、目標文件與操作決定是否拒絕。
備份處理復原，不替代存取控制。

en.prompt: Xiaoming and Xiaomei can both sign in, but Xiaomei tries to read Xiaoming’s private document. Which mechanism should primarily decide whether to deny access?
rationales: HTTPS protects transport; it does not decide access to each document.
Identifying a user does not grant access to another person’s documents.
C: authorization evaluates the identity, target document and requested operation.
Backups support recovery rather than access control.

zh.prompt: 假設兩位承辦人同時修改同一份資料，其中一人的內容被另一人覆蓋。主要是哪一類問題？
rationales: A：這是並行操作中的更新遺失，需要版本衝突等控制。
憑證不會協調同時修改的資料版本。
密碼強度不決定更新如何合併或拒絕。
配色無法修正資料競爭。

en.prompt: Two administrators edit the same record and one person’s content is overwritten. What kind of problem is this?
rationales: A: lost updates are a concurrency issue requiring controls such as version-conflict detection.
Certificates do not coordinate record versions.
Password strength does not determine how updates are combined or rejected.
Colors do not resolve data races.

zh.prompt: AI 已完成文件缺漏檢查功能，也成功部署到網址。現在可以宣布十人共用版完成嗎？
options: 可以，有網址就是正式系統
可以，只要 UI 做得漂亮
還不行，必須驗證多人權限、資料、協作與維護需求
rationales: 網址只提供連線入口，不能證明多人需求。
介面外觀不代替授權、持久化或維護證據。
C：需有相稱的多人操作、資料保存／還原及維護驗證證據。

en.prompt: AI completed the missing-document feature and deployed it at a URL. Is the ten-user version complete?
options: Yes; a URL makes it a production system.
Yes, if the UI looks polished.
Not yet; multi-user permissions, data, collaboration and maintenance requirements need verification.
rationales: A URL is an entry point, not evidence for shared-use requirements.
Appearance does not replace authorization, persistence or maintenance evidence.
C: proportionate evidence is needed for multi-user operations, persistence/recovery and maintenance.
